calls.head: Tired legs for the Jets
calls.body: The Jets played last night and get no rest before this one. Teams in that spot usually get the worse of the chances, so we expect the Panthers to control more of the play than they usually do.

calls.body: The Panthers’ power play is near the top of the league, and the Jets’ kill is near the bottom. Every trip to the box hurts the Jets more than most.

calls.title: The Panthers’ power play did its job
calls.plain: The Panthers’ power play created at least its usual chances. Florida went 2 for 5 on the power play.
calls.said: the Panthers’ power play would get its usual chances against the Jets’ shaky kill
calls.beyond: Florida has a better power play than most. Even by those standards, this was a big night: 16.3 expected goals per 60 on the power play, against their usual 8.6 (about 9.1 against Winnipeg) and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

FLA.head: We gave Florida a 69% chance, and they delivered.

WPG.head: We gave Winnipeg only a 31% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Winnipeg’s shots went from harmless to more harmless
surprises.body: Winnipeg usually gets some of the league’s least dangerous shots, and Florida usually allows fewer dangerous shots than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a night of harmless shots: Winnipeg’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 3.6% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 5.9% and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

story.head: Lundell lights the lamp for a hat trick
paras: Bokondji Imama and Tyrel Bauer dropped the gloves early in the first, and Sam Reinhart struck first for the Panthers on the power play late in the period. Anton Lundell stretched the lead to 2-0 early in the second. Winnipeg had a goal taken off on a challenge early in the period. Kyle Connor got the Jets on the board on the power play midway through the period. Seth Jones made it 3-1 for the Cats on the power play late in the period. Morgan Barron pulled the Jets within one midway through the third, but that was as close as they got. Lundell scored his second of the night with less than seven minutes left to make it 4-2 for the Panthers. Lundell completed his hat trick into the empty net with less than two minutes left. Jones finished with a goal and two assists.

The Panthers had a bit more of the good stuff, outshooting the Jets 38-24. Akira Schmid made 22 saves for the Panthers, and Nico Daws stopped 33 of 37 at the other end. The Panthers moved to 8-4-2, climbing to third in the Atlantic. The Jets are seventh in the Central. The Jets are winless in eight (0-6-2).

items.text: Three straight wins for the Panthers.
The Jets scored on the power play for the first time since Oct 15, after going 0-for-16 over six games.
Morgan Barron scored his first goal of the season, his first since Mar 21 (18 games played since).
The Panthers have won both meetings this season.
